title: Dualizing module and finite-support exclusion on a proper reduced curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be a nonempty proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. There exists a coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module $\omega_C$ [pqf-def-coherent], called its dualizing module, with a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(\mathcal F,\omega_C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(C,\mathcal F),k)$$
for every coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module $\mathcal F$, where module maps and cohomology are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. The pair consisting of $\omega_C$ and this natural isomorphism determines $\omega_C$ up to the unique isomorphism respecting it. For every generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the stalk $(\omega_C)_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is one-dimensional over the field $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$. Every coherent submodule of $\omega_C$ whose stalks at all these generic points are zero is zero. Equivalently, a morphism of coherent modules to $\omega_C$ is zero if all its component-generic stalk maps are zero. Finally,
$$\chi(C,\omega_C)=-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$$
for the Euler characteristic of [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. No connectedness, smoothness, geometric reducedness or condition $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), (2),(5); 0BS3 (lemma-duality-dim-1-CM), (1),(2),(4); 0BS5 (lemma-euler), second identity. Reduced pure-dimensional-one specialization; generic-field rank and exclusion of zero-dimensional submodules spell out the Cohen-Macaulay module assertion.

proof.text: Write $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Properness includes finite type. Thus $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is flat over the field by [lem-pc-flat-field]. On affine charts finite type over the Noetherian field implies finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-flat-dualizing-polynomial-model] to obtain the right adjoint $f^!$ and set $K=f^!k[0]$. By [lem-sfb-proper-field-algebraic-dualizing], $K$ has bounded coherent cohomology and every stalk is an algebraic dualizing complex.

source.place: Tag 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), proof: construction of the proper adjoint complex.

proof.text: Every local ring has dimension at most one: its prime chains give chains in an affine open of $C$. Reducedness and [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced] give depth at least $\min(1,\dim A)=\dim A$; the opposite inequality is [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] applied to $M=A$. Hence every local ring is Cohen–Macaulay. At a closed point $x$ the dimension is one: a zero-dimensional local ring would make $x$ generic for an irreducible component, and a closed generic point gives a zero-dimensional component, contrary to pure dimension one. The prime/local-point correspondence used here is [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization].

source.place: Tag 0BS3 (lemma-duality-dim-1-CM), hypotheses; reduced dimension-one argument in Tag 0E33 proof.

proof.text: At every closed point $x$, [lem-sfb-proper-dualizing-closed-stalk-normalized] normalizes $K_x$ and [lem-sfb-normalized-cm-local-dualizing-concentration] with $d=1$ gives $K_x\cong H^{-1}(K_x)[1]$. Therefore $H^j(K)_x=0$ for $j\ne-1$, using exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. Each coherent $H^j(K)$ has closed support by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. The space $C$ is quasi-compact by properness and Kolmogorov by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]: two points with the same closure would be two generic points of that irreducible closed subset. Thus [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] gives a closed point in any nonempty support, a contradiction. Thus $K$ is concentrated in degree $-1$. Put $\omega=H^{-1}(K)$; it is coherent, and [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] gives $K\cong\omega[1]$ in the derived category.

source.place: Tags 0BS2 and 0BS3: concentration and dualizing module.

proof.text:
For coherent $F$, the fully faithful degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], the isomorphism $K\cong\omega[1]$, and the adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F,\omega)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(C)}(F[1],K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k)}(R\Gamma(C,F)[1],k[0])=\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(C,F),k).$$
The last equality is the degreewise Hom bijection of [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting]: only degree zero of the target contributes, and $H^0(R\Gamma(F)[1])=H^1(C,F)$. All three comparisons are natural and $k$-linear; on the last Hom group a map is sent to its cohomology map.

The representing pair is unique by the following explicit argument. For two pairs, their duality maps give natural bijections $T_F:\operatorname{Hom}(F,\omega)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,\omega')$. Set $u=T_\omega(1)$ and $v=T_{\omega'}^{-1}(1)$. Naturality gives $T_F(h)=u\circ h$; applying this and its inverse to identities gives $vu=1$ and $uv=1$. Any isomorphism respecting the representing maps equals $T_\omega(1)=u$. This uses only coherent test modules, including the two representing modules.

source.place: Tag 0BS2, uniqueness footnote (Yoneda argument written out).

proof.text:
For a component-generic point $\eta$, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions](1), on an affine neighbourhood, makes $F=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ a field. Put $V=\omega_\eta$. Steps 1 and 3 give $K_\eta\cong V[1]$ and the scalar-action isomorphism $F[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_F(K_\eta,K_\eta)$ [lem-sfb-proper-field-algebraic-dualizing]. Compute this Hom using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. By [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting], every acyclic $F$-complex $A$ is contractible, say $1_A=dh+hd$. For any chain map $f:A\to V[1]$, the maps $fh$ give a null homotopy, since $f(dh+hd)=d(fh)+(fh)d$. Thus $V[1]$ itself is K-injective by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The derived-Hom definition permits this target model, giving the $F$-linear identification
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_F(V[1],V[1])=\operatorname{Hom}_F^\bullet(V[1],V[1])=\operatorname{End}_F(V)[0].$$
The complex has only degree zero and zero differential; the homothety sends $a$ to $a\,1_V$. Hence $F\to\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ is an $F$-linear isomorphism. In particular $V\ne0$, since otherwise $F\cong0$. Fix $v\ne0$. For each $w\in V$, [lem-sfb-linear-map-extension-prescribed-value] with $P=0$, $U=V$ gives $g\in\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ with $g(v)=w$. Surjectivity of homothety gives $g=a\,1_V$, so $w=av$. Therefore $v$ is a basis of $V$ and $\dim_FV=1$.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), proof: generic invertibility; Tag 0BS2 construction; scalar-action definition in dualizing.tex Tag 0A7B (definition-dualizing), with the field K-injective computation written out.

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq\omega$ be coherent with all component-generic stalks zero. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] and has dimension at most zero: any strict chain of two points in that support, preceded by a component-generic point of $C$, would give a chain of length two in $C$; the first point cannot already be generic since all generic stalks vanish. Apply [lem-pc-zero-support-finite-scheme] with the trivial invertible module to write $N=i_*G$ on a finite affine $k$-scheme, with $H^1(C,N)=H^1(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)=0$ by [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing]. Step 4 gives $\operatorname{Hom}(N,\omega)=0$. Thus the inclusion is zero, so $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E3E, proof: exclusion of modules supported in closed points; alternative direct use of Tag 0BS2 (5).

proof.text: For a map $F\to\omega$ of coherent modules, its image is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (image is the kernel of its coherent cokernel). Exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](4) identifies the image stalks with the images of the stalk maps. If all component-generic maps vanish, step 7 annihilates this image, so the map is zero. Conversely apply this assertion to the inclusion of a coherent submodule to recover step 7.

source.place: Tag 0E3E proof, finite-support exclusion as a morphism criterion.

proof.text:
Apply the adjunction to $\mathcal O_C[1-j]$ for each integer $j$. The structure-sheaf Hom identification [lem-pc-derived-structure-sheaf-hom-hypercohomology] and field-complex splitting [lem-trf-field-complex-cohomology-splitting] give
$$H^j(C,\omega)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^{1-j}(C,\mathcal O_C),k).$$
For $j=0,1$ these swap $H^0$ and $H^1$. For $j>1$ the right side vanishes because a module in degree zero has no negative derived global cohomology (its injective resolution begins in degree zero). For $j<0$ the left side vanishes for the same reason, so field splitting also gives $H^i(C,\mathcal O_C)=0$ for $i>1$. Finiteness is [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] and dual dimensions agree by [lem-sfb-linear-dual-dimension-rank]. Hence
$$\chi(C,\omega)=h^1(C,\mathcal O_C)-h^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C).$$
The calculation uses the whole space $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)$, without identifying it with $k$.
